TQ-12.3-01.description: The committed top-anchor status-pill reservation test could not fail when the reservation was removed.
TQ-12.3-01.detail: BadgeSizePositionTests.TopAnchorsReserveTheFirstRowForAWideStatusBand (BadgeSizePositionTests.cs:229-261) uses a deliberate wide probe (status text 70 px -> 94 px pill; the single technical pill 876 px text -> 900 px pill on a 1000x1500 poster, Medium). The reserved first row is safeWidth - statusWidth - pillGap = 952 - 94 - 8 = 850 px, so the 900 px technical pill cannot fit row 0 and must drop to row 1 (y = inset + pillHeight + rowGap = 80 >= status.Y + status.Height = 72); row 1 has full safeWidth 952 and holds it. The test asserts non-overlap, pill.Y >= status.Y + status.Height, and safe-area containment for both pills. Independently reproduced on a throwaway copy: replacing BadgeLayoutEngine.cs:86 'rowAvailableWidth[0] = safeWidth - statusPill.Width - pillGap;' with 'rowAvailableWidth[0] = safeWidth;' rebuilds clean and fails both TopLeft and TopRight cases at line 252 (Failed 2, Passed 1, Total 3), while the Center fact still passes.

TQ-12.3-03.description: The Center-anchor status-band row-reduction branch was never exercised.
TQ-12.3-03.detail: BadgeSizePositionTests.CenterAnchorStatusBandDropsTheRowsThatWouldStartInsideIt (BadgeSizePositionTests.cs:139-156) uses a 1000x240 poster where a 2-row centered block would start at (240 - 104)/2 = 68, inside the 80 px top status band (inset 24 + pill height 48 + row gap 8). The Center reduction drops availableRows to 1, so the block top becomes (240 - 48)/2 = 96 and only three technical pills are placed, all in row 0 at y = 96 >= status.Y + status.Height = 72. Independently reproduced on the same throwaway copy: changing BadgeLayoutEngine.cs:92 'CenteredBlockTop(...) < statusReserve' to '< -1' rebuilds clean and fails the Center fact with 'Expected 3, Actual 6' at line 150 (Failed 1, Passed 2, Total 3), while the reservation theory still passes. The two mutations are mutually independent, so each test pins its own branch.

TQ-12.3-02.description: The ADR-019 clause 6 identity-neutral default fingerprints have no unguarded absolute pin.
TQ-12.3-02.detail: Not addressed by attempt 4. The test-quality-reviewer's recommended action explicitly permits acceptance and assigns closure to task 12.4's coordinated schema/RenderVersion advance and golden regeneration; the worker report and PLANS.md carry the 12.3/12.4 handoff. The production default remains identity-neutral by construction (RenderFingerprint.cs:71-79 and RendererConfigurationFingerprint.cs:66-76 append only when Position != BottomLeft or Size != Medium), and production source is unchanged, so this is a test-strength residual, not a functional defect.
